Scenarios.Scenario: Open, restore, or switch an Integrated Browser editor with recent URL history.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing input resolution and browser-model initialization precede the added synchronous history refresh, existing layout, and awaited setVisible. The refresh reads cached workspace storage and creates at most one small recent-URL list per browser editor pane; persistence is not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize or retrieve the main-process browser view, position it, and update visibility.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initialization request per newly resolved model; existing layout and visibility requests per editor setup. None per recent URL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same input resolution, browser-view initialization, layout, and visibility calls occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initialization and setVisible remain on editor setup's critical path; the diff adds only bounded local UI work before visibility.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Use the existing persistent or ephemeral Electron session and create a browser view on a model miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per new browser-view ID; persistent sessions are shared according to the existing storage scope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical browser/session creation path before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of existing cold browser initialization, not triggered by enumerating history entries.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Up to 10 normally persisted URL entries, initially displaying 3; one browser editor pane per editor group rather than one history widget per open tab.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Editor setup resumes on the renderer event loop. BrowserEditorInput shares its pending resolve promise and the workbench service reuses models by ID. No new parallel browser creation or per-URL requests are added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Missing history returns an empty list without creating a List widget. Existing history is JSON-parsed from the storage service's in-memory map. Cold browser models use the existing initialization IPC; warm models are reused. Input changes clear the input-owned disposables, and ListView.dispose clears items and removes its DOM node.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced editor setup, model reuse, cached storage reads, bounded list contents, and widget disposal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings are supplied. Costs vary with URL lengths and number of editor groups, but the normal history cardinality is explicitly capped at 10.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance regression: added setup work is a bounded local history widget, not eager loading of the recorded pages or per-entry IPC.

Scenarios.Scenario: Navigate from the address bar and record the final URL, including redirected navigation.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing loadURL IPC starts navigation. After did-navigate, the added handler updates history and synchronously refreshes subscribed browser panes. Storage flushes are asynchronous and are not awaited before navigation can progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward one requested navigation to Electron webContents.loadURL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One loadURL request per user navigation, independent of history size.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Address-bar navigation already issued the same loadURL IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing navigation operation is awaited; the new history work runs on the navigation event without issuing another loadURL.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the requested document, redirects, and its resources using Chromium.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One page navigation with site-dependent resource requests; storing history does not fetch any recorded URLs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical page and resource loading before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Network latency remains the existing navigation critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse and stringify the workspace recent-URL array.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most 10 entries per normal mutation; one addition and at most one effective removal per recorded navigation, plus a bounded parse per subscribed pane refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Added synchronous renderer work in the navigation-event handler, bounded by the history cap.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist coalesced storage updates through the existing storage channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One batched request per flush, not one request per history entry or subscribed pane. First insertion can also update the storage-target metadata key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No browser-recent-history key was written; the same batching infrastructure already served other workspace storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the navigation critical path; the history service does not await persistence.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the bounded history value in the existing workspace database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The latest pending value for the single history key is flushed with other storage changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No history value was persisted; the workspace database and its storage lifecycle already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous, delayed persistence rather than synchronous per-URL disk access.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One history addition per pending user navigation, optionally preceded by removal when the original URL differs and exists. Each history contains at most 10 entries. Refresh fan-out is to subscribed browser editor panes, not all browser tabs or history entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: History mutations and event delivery are synchronous on the renderer event loop. Storage coalesces updates by key with a 100 ms ThrottledDelayer; its Throttler permits one active flush and coalesces queued work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration and storage reads are local. Each mutation parses the small cached history and serializes the capped replacement. Missing original URLs do not save or emit a removal event. Redirect removal and addition update the same pending storage key and normally share a flush.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the navigation callback, conditional removal, 10-entry write cap, synchronous event fan-out, cached reads, storage IPC, and flush coalescing/serialization.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual URL byte lengths, page load duration, and number of subscribed panes vary. There is no evidence that the bounded history processing produces a material navigation slowdown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: persistence uses existing delayed/coalesced storage, there is no per-entry network or IPC fan-out, and local history processing is small and capped.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use the welcome-page history: expand/collapse, open a URL, open it in a background tab, remove an entry, or clear history.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Expand/collapse rebuilds the bounded local list. Opening an entry uses the normal navigation or editor-resolution path. Removal and clearing update local storage and refresh subscribed lists immediately, with persistence deferred.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Navigate the current browser or resolve/create a background browser input after explicit selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected URL per activation; at most one model initialization for a newly resolved background input.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The history activation surface did not exist, but opening the same URL manually already used these browser/editor services with the same per-activation work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Normal browser initialization/navigation determines time to display the selected page; no such boundary is crossed by expand/collapse or rendering the list.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the one explicitly selected page through Chromium.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One navigation per selected entry, not one navigation per rendered history item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No welcome-page history activation existed; equivalent manual navigation performed the same fetch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the selected page's normal navigation critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Flush the updated or removed history key through the existing batched storage pipeline.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pending key update/deletion per mutation, coalesced within the storage flush window; no per-URL persistence call on clear.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No recent-history mutation commands or associated storage writes existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Deferred and not awaited by the UI mutation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Three collapsed entries or up to 10 expanded entries, with a 300 px viewport. Each explicit activation opens one URL; list rendering never opens all entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: List updates and selection events run synchronously. Full list splices without an identity provider clear selection, and the empty-selection handler returns, so history refresh does not recursively navigate. Background-tab resolution shares the existing input resolve promise; there is no collection-wide creation burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: History comes from cached workspace storage; no per-item service reads. Existing lists and the toggle Link are reused during refresh. Renderer listener stores are cleared on row rerender, and input-owned widgets/listeners are disposed on input replacement or clearing. Empty history disposes the current list.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected list trait splicing, selection handling, list/link reuse, rendering listener cleanup, widget disposal, and the existing background input resolver.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of user interactions and editor groups varies; the history collection and rendered viewport remain small. No measurements establish a material UI cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance bug: operations remain bounded and user-triggered, with no navigation loop, unbounded history retention, or eager loading of recent pages.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Recent URLs Settings or disable remembering recent URLs.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new menu command calls the existing preferences service once with an exact setting query. The preferences service forces the graphical settings editor for query-based opens and opens its cached input. The remembering check is a synchronous configuration lookup before adding history.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the standard graphical settings editor with an exact-ID query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cached editor input/open per user command, unrelated to history length.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The new history menu shortcut did not exist; the existing Browser Settings action already used the same preferences-service path for a different query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only blocks the explicitly requested settings view; no settings initialization is added to browser startup or navigation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One command invocation and one configuration key, independent of recent-history cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One ordinary settings-editor open per explicit command; no per-entry tasks or new background workers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: PreferencesService uses createOrGetCachedSettingsEditor2Input. The delayed browser service registration is unchanged. Disabled remembering returns before parsing or writing history in addRecentUrl.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the new command's scheduling and cardinality: traced the preferences-service entry point, forced graphical-editor branch, and cached editor input.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold graphical settings-editor initialization duration is not measured; its implementation and frequency are not amplified by this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: settings work is explicit, singular, and uses the existing cached preferences workflow.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all seven changed files and every diff page. Investigated navigation and history cardinality, storage caching and asynchronous persistence, UI/list lifecycle and selection behavior, background-tab model resolution, and settings-command scheduling. No concrete actionable performance regression or performance-regression fix was established; no findings submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
